title: The Tale of the Church of the SubGenius
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the Church of the SubGenius, the absurdist parody religion founded in Dallas in the late 1970s by Ivan Stang and Philo Drummond. They cover the Bob Dobbs clip-art face, the founders' origins and early CB radio work, the Hour of Slack, core concepts like slack, the conspiracy, pinks and YETIs, original and involuntary slack, the Rewardian and Emergent Tile approaches, the anti-music and devivals, the staged assassinations and the 1990s schism, the Boston show canceled after a Columbine reference, the documentary that broke character, and the church's fading and later revival. The episode ends with a listener correction about William the Conqueror and the Magna Carta episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and introductions to the Church of the SubGenius
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Church of the SubGenius, the Bob Dobbs clip-art image, and two definitions of the church from Steve Davis and Ed the Grabster, calling it an absurdist in-joke and parody of a religion.

segments.title: Founders Ivan Stang and Philo Drummond
segments.summary: Stang and Drummond, outsiders in Dallas, meet through a friend, bond over comics, Frank Zappa and Captain Beefheart, and collect extremist pamphlets, including Jack Chick tracts.

segments.title: Creating a fake religion and the L. Ron Hubbard influence
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the appeal of inventing a religion, Josh's experience writing a pilot about a fake religion, and how the founders were fascinated by L. Ron Hubbard and Scientology without wanting to exploit people, plus the nine-dollar joke attributed to Stang.

segments.title: Dollar donations and the nature of the mailings
segments.summary: Stang makes a modest living from mail orders and still stuffs envelopes and sends pamphlets and CDs. The hosts argue that donors are in on the joke and sending money out of gratitude.

segments.title: Origin story: subgeniuses and the first pamphlet
segments.summary: Stang's realization that they were not geniuses but subgeniuses sparked the idea. They spent sixty dollars on the first pamphlet and sent it to publishers, who rejected it until McGraw Hill eventually accepted.

segments.title: Pamphlet doctrine, Jehovah One, and the CB radio beginnings
segments.summary: The hosts describe the pamphlet's doomsday headlines, the Bob Dobbs character channeling Jehovah One, and how the founders trolled on CB radio, which led to the Hour of Slack and the terms pinks and pink boys.

segments.title: Pinks, YETIs, and the SubGenius identity
segments.summary: The hosts explain the categories of pinks, people who are sold on the conspiracy, and SubGenii of YETI heritage, who are aware of Bob's teachings and work against the conspiracy.

segments.title: Bob Dobbs clip art origin and trademark joke
segments.summary: The Bob Dobbs face comes from a clip art catalog. The church's website notes it is trademarked, which the hosts find hard to read as joke or real.

segments.title: Slack, the conspiracy, original and involuntary slack
segments.summary: The hosts define slack as contentment with minimal exertion, using a toilet-brush anecdote as a non-slack example. They describe the conspiracy acronym, false or manufactured slack, original slack, and involuntary slack such as getting fired.

segments.title: Rewardians versus Emergent Tiles
segments.summary: The two philosophies of slack are compared. Rewardians slack off, while Emergent Tiles find slack in self-set goals, with the hosts comparing the Rewardian approach to the film Dazed and Confused's Wooderson-like character.

segments.title: Devivals, anti-music, and the Spinal Tap comparison
segments.summary: The hosts describe devivals with mock evangelical preaching and anti-music jam sessions, and compare attending a live show to seeing Spinal Tap in concert. Mottoes include fum and the joke-is-the-point line.

segments.title: Staged assassinations, the 1990s schism, and the Boston show
segments.summary: The church's staged assassinations and the scripted schism between the Holocaustles and Evangelicals are described, along with the San Francisco theater shows, a fan who took it seriously, and the Boston show canceled after a Columbine reference and bomb threats.

segments.title: Documentary, decline, revival, and further reading
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the documentary by Sandy Boone in which Stang and Drummond break character, the church's decline and revival online, the 2020s political fringe, and recommend Reverend Nancy Regalia's essay on gender.
